title: Losing at dice at the Smart Set Social Club
summary: Paid five dollars for a gig, he gambled upstairs, lost it, was kicked down the stairs by the caretaker and never gambled again.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: had to forget that. So now I'm playing my gigs and things are running smooth. So they had a little gathering up on the second floor, called the Smart Set Social Club, so I said I'm going up here and try my hand out in the gambling. I went up there and they paid me $5.00 for that gig and I said, there wasn't nobody up there but the caretaker,whatever he was and this man had hands about 10 inches long and the stick was almost that long. He said, all right, then, here we go. I said $1.00. I threw them dice on 12, so I was ready to ride. On 2, 2 again, 12, then 2. I said that's life, that's the way you do it.
So when I got to the stairs that man put his foot all of the way up in my derriere and I come all the way down those stairs. He said if you ever come in again, I will -- you know.

Now, from U Street, from 11th and U to 22nd and E, first you got to go all the way to 11th, you got 11 blocks to go, long blocks, Washington blocks to go and then you got to come down from U to E Street, so I made that -- I never had any desire to try to gamble, never, so I'm happy about that. I am extremely happy.
